what: Teva is the world's largest maker of generic medicines, and also sells branded products: Austedo for movement disorders, Ajovy for migraine and Uzedy for schizophrenia. It is Israeli and sells in 57 markets.
customers: Pharmacies, wholesalers, hospitals and health systems worldwide.
money: off-patent medicines across the US, Europe and other markets
moat: The scale to manufacture thousands of generic products at low cost, plus branded medicines with patent protection that fund the business.
risks: Debt of about $17 billion against $4 billion of cash, left from the Actavis purchase
It pays no dividend while repaying that debt
Generic drug pricing in the United States is under constant pressure
Opioid litigation settlements continue to consume cash
opportunities: Austedo has been growing quickly and is the main profit engine
A late-stage pipeline in immunology and neuroscience
Biosimilars are a higher-margin area where it has scale
watch: Austedo revenue growth and the pace of debt reduction.
